- If sentiment is strongly bullish (≥0.67) in recent days, model tends to underpredict sharp upward moves; adjust forecast upward by 1–3% for the next 5–7 days.
- If sentiment is strongly bearish (≤0.33) or shows sudden negative spikes, model often overpredicts downward trend; increase forecast by 2–5% to counteract mean reversion bias.
- After a sharp spike in price (e.g., >5% from prior day), model frequently overreacts and forecasts continued steep rise; cap forecast slope at 1–2% per day until sentiment stabilizes.
- When sentiment shifts from bullish to bearish (or vice versa) within 3–5 days, model often lags by 1–3 days; adjust forecast to align with sentiment shift 1–2 days ahead.
- If model consistently forecasts flat or slightly rising prices while true outcome shows strong mean reversion (e.g., 3–5 consecutive days of decline), reduce forecast slope by 0.5–1.5% per day.
- For 30-day horizon, if true outcome shows early volatility followed by consolidation, model often overestimates early peak; reduce forecast peak by 2–4% and shift peak to later days if sentiment remains neutral or slightly bullish.
